newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends off on Iraq oil factor, SPR news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends off on Iraq oil factor, SPR news.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended lower Tuesday on talk of new supply as Iraq expressed hope its oil-for-food deal may be implemented soon and oil sales from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve were approved by the U.S. Senate.

"Crude opened down sharply on the Iraq news, but it's the same people who are hopeful, that have been hopeful for months," said John Saucer, an analyst with Smith Barney, adding implementation of the deal would need the support of the United States which it currently does not have.
November crude oil settled off 24 cents at $24.14 a barrel after falling as low as $23.83.
November heating oil settled up a mere 0.01 cent to 70.76 cents a gallon while November gasoline settled up 0.56 cent to 62.82 cents a gallon.

Iraq's Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf said on Tuesday he saw a consensus among foreign ministers at a UN General Assembly meeting in New York for a speedy implementation of the oil-for food deal.

Under the deal, trade sanctions imposed on Iraq over its 1990 invasion of Kuwait would be eased by the United Nations, and Iraq would be allowed to export $2 billion of oil over six months in exchange for humanitarian aid.
"This oil deal is just not going to go through before the (presidential) election," a trader said.

Crude also came under pressure after the U.S. Senate late Monday approved a move to sell $220 million worth of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to help close the budget gap in a spending bill for the 1997 fiscal year.

Refined product prices rose after a refinery fire at a Conoco refinery in Louisiana ignited buying in gasoline amid trader talk the company shut its 51,000 barrel per day (bpd) cat cracker at the Lake Charles plant.
But the company said that while three workers were injured in the Monday evening blaze, refinery operations were unaffected at the 180,000 bpd refinery.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
